newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia arrests more suspects in Timor killing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia arrests more suspects in Timor killing.

text.p: Indonesian police said on Thursday they had detained 15 suspects in the killing of a soldier in pre-Christmas violence in East Timor and were hunting for 12 others, the official Antara news agency reported.
"The 15 men who attacked Corporal Alfredo dos Santos during the riot are under detention," East Timor police chief Colonel Jusuf Muharam said in Dili, the territory's capital.
He said police were still searching for 12 other suspects in the killing of dos Santos, also known as Siga. Antara gave no other details.

Dos Santos was beaten to death near Dili's cathedral on December 24. On the same day, several other police and soldiers were attacked by members of the crowd welcoming Nobel Peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo back to the territory.
Belo has publicly apologised for the death of the soldier, a native East Timorese and father of seven.
Muharam said 29 other people were being questioned by the police as witnesses in the disturbance.
"However, it is also possible for these witnesses to become suspects in this case," he said without elaborating.
East Timor Deputy Police Chief Atok Rismanto told Reuters earlier this month that suspects would be charged with property damage, assault and murder.
Indonesian troops invaded the former Portuguese colony in December 1975 and East Timor was incorporated as Indonesia's 27th province the following July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
